title: Ballistic Speed and Potential-Theoretic Recurrence for Homogeneous Open Quantum Random Walks
authors: Ameur Dhahri, Chul Ki Ko, Farrukh Mukhamedov, Hyun Jae Yoo
abstract: Our study connects root-mean-square ballistic transport to potential-theoretic recurrence for finite-range open quantum random walks. In homogeneous walks with primitive local channels, finitely many simple periodic Fourier peripheral eigenvalues, no nonzero stationary Fourier mode, and a nondegenerate quadratic spectral term, we prove a periodic uniform local limit theorem and recover exponential finite-set return bounds for nonzero drift. The centered case yields strong Green-function asymptotics in at least three dimensions, as well as potential-kernel asymptotics in one and two dimensions. According to these assumptions, the RMS ballistic speed equals the drift norm, nonzero drift indicates transience, and centered walks are recurring in effective dimensions one and two but transitory in higher dimensions. The low-dimensional finding shows a recurrence of the origin projection in TOM. For reducible walks, an explicit harmonic \(h\)-transform converts each absorption component to an OQRW, providing a detailed breakdown of Green occupation potentials. The squared RMS speed is the absorption-weighted mean of squared component drifts, but the reduced drift-dimension classification also needs specific component return estimations. A centered noncommuting family validates the fundamental spectral assumptions in all dimensions and provides explicit potential constants. Exact finite traps and sparse reflecting barriers provide a complementary nonhomogeneous method for zero speed and TOM recurrence.
summary: This paper rigorously connects the macroscopic transport properties (ballistic speed) of Open Quantum Random Walks to their underlying potential-theoretic recurrence behavior. It establishes that the speed is determined by the drift norm, while recurrence depends on the effective dimension of the walk. The findings are vital for understanding how dissipation affects quantum transport in open systems.
main_problem: The study connects the root-mean-square (RMS) ballistic transport of Open Quantum Random Walks (OQRWs) to their potential-theoretic recurrence properties.
main_result: The ballistic speed equals the drift norm, and the recurrence behavior (transience vs. recurrence) is determined by the effective dimension of the walk, showing recurrence in effective dimensions one and two for centered walks.
method: The analysis employs spectral theory, potential theory, and component decomposition to analyze the asymptotic behavior of the Green function and the walk's position moments.
model_or_system: The model is the Open Quantum Random Walk (OQRW), which describes dissipative quantum dynamics using positive local channels, contrasting with unitary quantum walks.
key_observables: RMS ballistic speed ($v_{bal}$), recurrence (state-dependent vs. TOM sense), average drift, and Green function asymptotics.
important_parameters: Effective lattice dimension, drift norm, and the spectral properties of the local channels.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires assumptions such as homogeneous walks, primitive local channels, and non-degenerate quadratic spectral terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate aggregation laws in the reducible regime, showing linear decomposition for Green occupation potentials and averaging of squared component drifts for RMS transport.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing local limit theorems and then using component decomposition to separately analyze the ballistic speed (related to drift) and the recurrence properties (related to potential theory).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to analyze non-unitary, dissipative quantum dynamics, which is crucial for modeling open quantum systems interacting with an environment.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Local-to-global architecture of the main argument. The periodic local theorem controls time returns, while the centered resolvent singularity controls the spatial profile of Green functions and potential kernels.

Figure 2. Parity mask for the one-dimensional simple symmetric walk. The periodic local theorem retains both peripheral Fourier points and produces the factor two on the admissible parity class, rather than imposing strong aperiodicity.
Figure 3. Drift–effective-dimension classification in the primitive one-component regime. RMS speed detects drift, whereas recurrence also depends on the rank of the effective lattice.

Figure 4. Two different aggregation laws in the reducible regime. Green occupa- tion potentials decompose linearly, whereas RMS transport averages the squared component drifts. A drift–dimension criterion for the component Green series additionally requires Assumption 5.3.
